SMTO-EXE-0186 — Too many cells for one step

GUID: 5cc57a2c-5749-572e-9c82-f35434743691
Slug: office-range-too-large
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO can work with at most 4,096 cells, and at most 256 columns, in one spreadsheet or Word table step. This request asked for more than that, so nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to split the work into blocks, for example 100 rows at a time when there are 40 columns (4,000 cells). Each block then stays under the 4,096-cell limit for a single step.
  2. Keep each block to 256 columns or fewer, for example columns A to IV. SMTO also limits how wide one spreadsheet area can be.
  3. When SMTO is done, open the final copy and check that the first and last rows are all there. Working in blocks is safe only if none of the blocks were skipped.

What success looks like

  • Each block finishes, and the final copy of the file contains all of your data.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the number of rows and columns you need, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An Office request exceeded the per-operation cell limits: a range or values grid over 4,096 cells, an Excel range wider than 256 columns, or a Word table over 4,096 cells.

What this means

  • A selected range/value matrix exceeded 4,096 cells or an Excel range exceeded 256 columns. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • A selected range/value matrix exceeded 4,096 cells or an Excel range exceeded 256 columns.

How to diagnose it

  • Count the requested cells/columns and ensure that splitting preserves the intended edit and source revision checks.

How to fix it

  • Split the work into ranges of at most 4,096 cells and 256 columns each (for example 100 rows by 40 columns), and send each as a separate operation against the latest output revision; Word tables created in one call are limited to 4,096 cells.
  • Split the operation into at most 4096 cells and 256 columns per range.

Retry and execution caution

  • Split the operation into at most 4096 cells and 256 columns per range.

How to verify the fix

  • Each deliberate operation fits its range bound and preserves all required data.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
